summary: access smoke: broker-level proof that durable deletion flips /readyz (or exits) — end-to-end for TKT-97
description: TKT-97 planning decision #4 (deferred to follow-up, owner-waived gateless run). TKT-97 unit-tested the *reaction* to ConsumeContext.Closed() firing (waitConsume) but not that the nats.go library actually fires Closed() on durable deletion — that needs a live NATS. Add a smoke test in the smoke/ module: start the access consumer against a real JetStream, delete the durable (access-ticket-issuer and/or access-slot-policy) via the NATS API, assert /readyz flips to 503 (or the process exits) within a bound. Larger harness than make check's unit gate (compose orchestration + durable manipulation), which is why it was split out of TKT-97. Confidence today rests on the library's documented Closed() contract (pull.go:803-808) + TKT-97's unit reaction test; this closes the loop end-to-end.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Born from TKT-97 planning open-decision #4 (E2E durable-kill test: now vs follow-up → follow-up). Code pointers: smoke/access_consumer_test.go (existing live-NATS access smoke to extend), services/access/internal/consumer/run.go (waitConsume, the reaction under test). Governing ADR: ADR-017 §256-259 (the 'loudly-unready on durable deletion' guarantee this would prove end-to-end).

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed from Ready. Branch `TKT-99-access-durable-deletion-smoke` off `origin/main` @ 25b7f6f.

**Selection reason.** Owner-directed run. TKT-99 is the deferred half of TKT-97 (planning
decision #4): TKT-97 shipped and unit-tested the *reaction* to `ConsumeContext.Closed()` firing
(`services/access/internal/consumer/run.go:waitConsume`), but nothing in the repo proves the
nats.go library actually fires `Closed()` when a durable is deleted out from under a live
consumer. Today's confidence is a documented library contract plus a unit test that fakes the
signal. This closes it end-to-end against a real JetStream. Zero open blockers (`links: []`).

**⚠️ GATELESS RUN — the four human gates are waived for this ticket by explicit repo-owner
directive, as a process experiment.** Recorded here so the board history shows it. Substitutions:

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | already given (ticket was in Ready) |
| 2 — plan approval | human approves the plan | orchestrator resolves open decisions itself: prefer the plan-critique's recommendation; absent one, the most reversible option. Every self-made decision + rationale recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews the PR and squash-merges | orchestrator squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules). Review-guide still posted on the PR first — it is the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates COS | orchestrator self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, then the full `kind=metrics` closeout. |

This is **not** `risk:low` — the label is absent and stays absent. A waived gate is a recorded
owner decision; `risk:low` is a claim about the work. Per `references/ab-stages.md` §`plan` rule 6,
a waived Gate 2 does **not** collapse the plan A/B: every arm runs and the orchestrator stands in
as judge, disclosing the arm mapping in the stage comment.

**Stop conditions still armed** (the run halts and reports instead of proceeding): gate/CI failing
twice on one cause with no clear fix; implementation reaching into auth, money paths, data
migrations or CI/deploy config beyond what the plan anticipated; a blocking finding surviving the
churn cap; a configured model unreachable after the documented escalation ladder; any ambiguous
destructive action.

**Model routing for this ticket** (`.claude/sdlc.config.json`, as it stands in the working tree):
`plan: ["gpt-5.6-sol"]` · `planReview: main-agent` · `implement: main-agent` ·
`aiReview: ["gpt-5.6-sol"]`. Both cross-model pairs are distinct (planner ≠ plan-reviewer,
implementer ≠ ai-reviewer), so the load-bearing invariant holds. Both A/B arrays are currently
**single-arm** — the A/B machinery runs but measures nothing; noted so the stage comments are not
read as a comparison.

**Governing ADR (re-resolved at claim time, not trusted from the mémo):** ADR-017 §5b —
§236-241 ("under Compose nothing acts on unhealthy … a visible red dot and no more"; parking never
self-heals) and §254-259 ("treat *recreate the durable consumer* as equivalent to a rollback"), the
paragraphs that make durable deletion a first-class operational event rather than an accident. The
mémo's `governingAdrs: ["ADR-017"]` was captured 2026-07-19 and still resolves; re-checked against
`docs/adr/` at HEAD. One consequence the drafter must not miss: because §236-238 says Compose does
**not** react to an unhealthy container, the only thing that actually removes a terminated access
process under `restart: unless-stopped` is the **process exit** — so "the red dot" and "the restart"
are two different observables with two different lifetimes, and which one a smoke test can see is a
design question, not a detail.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex companion, `task --effort high`, read-only — no working-tree writes). `config.models.plan` is a single-arm array, so the A/B machinery ran but measured nothing; this is one draft, not a comparison. Brief: ticket + COS candidates + ADR-017 §5b governing section + the real `run.go` / `consumer.go` / `policy.go` / `main.go` excerpts + the smoke-harness constraints (no access host port, `restart: unless-stopped`, source-order test sequencing, DeliverAll replay) + five named open decisions. Verbatim below; critique follows as `kind=plan-final`.

## 1. Approach

- Add one smoke test, `TestAccessPolicyDurableDeletionRestartsAndRecovers` (new), at the top of [smoke/access_consumer_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/smoke/access_consumer_test.go), before `TestAccessPoisonEventPolicy`.
- Establish positive controls: Access is ready, `access-slot-policy` exists with the expected configuration, and the container’s initial `RestartCount`, `StartedAt`, durable `Created`, and relevant log count are recorded.
- Delete `access-slot-policy` through `stream.DeleteConsumer`; do not simulate `ConsumeContext.Closed()`.
- Do not try to catch the transient `/readyz` 503. Assert the durable-specific `waitConsume` error and an automatic container restart within 15 seconds.
- Assert the recreated durable has a later `Created` timestamp and Access returns to ready with no pending policy replay within 20 seconds.
- Require two consecutive healthy/stable observations before returning.
- Register recovery cleanup before deletion so even an intentional RED mutation that prevents self-healing cannot poison later smoke tests.
- Keep the test in `make check`; it should normally add only one fast container restart.

## 2. Decisions

### D1 — Observable

**Recommendation:** use the exact termination diagnostic plus `RestartCount` and `StartedAt`. Use `/app healthcheck` only to prove recovery.

Required failure observations:

- The Access logs gain one occurrence of:

  ```text
  access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)
  ```

- `{{.RestartCount}}` becomes greater than its baseline.
- `{{.State.StartedAt}}` becomes later than its baseline.

A host port should not be added. It would expose another internal service and still would not make the 503 deterministic: the interval between `ready.Store(false)` and process exit is only a few goroutine scheduling turns. An in-network `docker exec ... /app healthcheck` has process-launch latency and cannot distinguish a 503 from connection failure once Access exits. Either probe could miss the entire window.

The restart is the durable observable ADR-017 expects Compose to act on. The exact error connects that restart to `waitConsume` rather than merely observing container churn.

### D2 — Durable

**Recommendation:** delete only `access-slot-policy`.

Reasons:

- It exercises the same `CreateOrUpdateConsumer` → `Consume` → `cc.Closed()` → `waitConsume` path as `access-ticket-issuer`.
- Replaying policy publications invokes `UpsertSlotPolicy`, which is idempotent by envelope ID in [services/access/internal/store/policy.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/policy.go).
- Placing the test before `TestAccessPoisonEventPolicy` means the isolated smoke stream should not yet contain catalog publications, so the normal gate replay is empty.
- Deleting `access-ticket-issuer` would replay all retained orders and revisit signed lifecycle issuance. That is materially more blast radius for no additional proof of nats.go’s `Closed()` behavior.
- Testing both would add a second restart and replay without covering a distinct library mechanism.

### D3 — Restoration

**Recommendation:** make restoration a hard test postcondition and back it with cleanup.

Before deletion, register cleanup that retains a usable NATS connection until cleanup completes. If either the durable is absent or `/app healthcheck` fails, cleanup must run:

```text
docker restart <project>-access-1
```

Then poll for up to 20 seconds until all are true:

- `stream.Consumer(..., "access-slot-policy")` and `Info` succeed.
- The durable has the expected filter, delivery, and acknowledgment policies.
- `NumPending == 0` and `NumAckPending == 0`.
- `docker exec <project>-access-1 /app healthcheck` exits zero.
- The container is running.

The normal assertion additionally requires the recreated consumer’s `Created` timestamp to be later than the pre-deletion value. Require the full condition twice, 500 milliseconds apart, with an unchanged `RestartCount`. This avoids returning during a brief healthy interval before another failure.

Cleanup must use its own bounded context and report both Access logs and container state if forced recovery fails.

### D4 — Gate placement

**Recommendation:** keep it in the default `make check`.

This test closes a dependency-level assumption on which Access liveness depends. Making it opt-in would leave ordinary changes to nats.go, consumer configuration, `waitConsume`, or process wiring unprotected.

The success path contains no fixed multi-second sleep. A 15-second reaction bound and 20-second restoration bound are failure ceilings; the expected warm path should finish in roughly 2–6 seconds. One lower-risk durable and one restart are proportionate to the coverage.

### D5 — Mutation resistance

**Recommendation:** require both the newly emitted exact diagnostic and a post-deletion restart.

A restart alone is insufficient. The discriminator is:

1. Capture the count of the exact `access-slot-policy` termination message in Access logs.
2. Successfully delete that live durable.
3. Require the count to increase.
4. Require `RestartCount` and `StartedAt` to advance afterward.
5. Require a newly created durable.

An unrelated crash can increment `RestartCount`, but it cannot produce the durable-specific `waitConsume` message and a replacement durable with a later `Created` timestamp.

C2 should be narrowed slightly: this smoke test pins delivery of `Closed()` and propagation of the distinctive termination error through `main`. The existing `TestWaitConsumeAsyncTerminationLatchesUnreadyAndErrors` in [services/access/internal/consumer/run_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/consumer/run_test.go) pins `ready.Store(false)`. Removing only that store is not reliably observable through HTTP before exit; the combined smoke and unit gate pins both halves.

## 3. Definition of done

### C1 — Live broker reaction

- A smoke test obtains the existing live `access-slot-policy` durable from `PLATFORM`.
- Access passes `/app healthcheck` before deletion.
- `stream.DeleteConsumer(ctx, "access-slot-policy")` succeeds against the real smoke JetStream.
- Within 15 seconds, the exact termination diagnostic appears and the Access container restarts.
- No mocked channel or direct invocation of `waitConsume` is used.

### C2 — Mutation-resistant behavior

Amended COS:

- Neutering the `closed` arm so it no longer returns the named termination error makes the new smoke test RED.
- Removing the arm entirely makes the test RED because neither the diagnostic nor automatic restart occurs.
- Removing only `ready.Store(false)` makes the existing TKT-97 unit test RED; this limitation is documented rather than papered over with a racy 503 poll.
- A random Access restart without the exact new diagnostic does not satisfy the smoke test.

### C3 — Stack recovery

Before the new test returns:

- The replacement `access-slot-policy` durable exists and is newer than the deleted instance.
- Its configuration still matches `SubjectPerformancePublished`, `DeliverAllPolicy`, `AckExplicitPolicy`, and `MaxDeliver: -1`.
- Its pending and acknowledgment-pending counts are zero.
- Access passes `/app healthcheck` in two consecutive stable samples.
- A cleanup fallback force-restarts Access and verifies the same healthy end-state if the main assertion exits early.
- `TestAccessPoisonEventPolicy` and all later smoke tests pass in the same package invocation.

### C4 — Gate and cost

- The new test runs without an environment guard under the existing smoke build tag.
- `make check` passes.
- A warm before/after measurement shows no more than approximately 10 seconds added to the smoke stage; investigate rather than accepting a larger regression.
- The test uses bounded polling, not a fixed long sleep.

## 4. Files

- [smoke/access_consumer_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/smoke/access_consumer_test.go)

  Add the new test before `TestAccessPoisonEventPolicy`. Add imports needed for Docker commands and numeric/time parsing. Any small polling or restoration helper introduced here must be clearly new, local to this file, return errors instead of calling `Fatal` from cleanup, and include command output in failures.

No changes are planned for:

- `compose.yaml`
- `compose.smoke.yaml`
- `scripts/smoke.sh`
- `smoke/smoke_test.go`
- Production Access code or ADRs

The existing `natsURL`, `project`, and `inspect` symbols are sufficient.

## 5. Test plan

### Test seam

1. Create a 45-second overall test context.
2. Connect to `natsURL`, construct JetStream, and obtain `PLATFORM`.
3. Resolve `access-slot-policy` and call `Info`.
4. Assert its exact consumer configuration.
5. Run `docker exec <project>-access-1 /app healthcheck`; require success.
6. Record:

   - Consumer `Created`.
   - Container `RestartCount`.
   - Container `StartedAt`.
   - Current count of the exact termination message in `docker compose -p <project> logs --no-color access`.

7. Register connection close and restoration cleanup in an order that keeps NATS usable during restoration.
8. Call `stream.DeleteConsumer(ctx, "access-slot-policy")`.
9. Poll every 250 milliseconds for at most 15 seconds until:

   - The exact diagnostic count has increased.
   - `RestartCount` is greater than baseline.
   - `StartedAt` is later than baseline.

10. Poll restoration for at most 20 seconds and require the stable conditions from C3 twice, 500 milliseconds apart.

On failure, include the baseline/current restart metadata, consumer lookup error, healthcheck result, and recent Access logs.

### Honest RED

Because TKT-99 is test-only, RED means demonstrating that the test rejects a broken version of the already-shipped behavior:

1. Add the smoke test.
2. Temporarily change the `case <-closed:` branch in [services/access/internal/consumer/run.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/consumer/run.go) to return `nil` without the distinctive error.
3. Rebuild the Access smoke binary and run the new test against a live isolated Compose stack.
4. Confirm the test fails because the exact diagnostic does not appear, even if `Run` subsequently exits through another error and Docker restarts it.
5. For the stronger mutation, temporarily make the `closed` arm wait for `ctx.Done()`; confirm the test times out waiting for both the diagnostic and automatic restart, while cleanup force-restarts Access and restores the durable.
6. Separately remove only `ready.Store(false)` and run `TestWaitConsumeAsyncTerminationLatchesUnreadyAndErrors`; confirm the existing unit test is RED.
7. Revert every temporary mutation.
8. Run the Access unit tests, the new smoke test in the real stack, and finally `make check`.

Do not commit any mutation used to establish RED.

## 6. Risks

- **The 503 is too short to observe.**  
  Mitigation: do not assert it. Assert the exact error and restart; use readiness only after recovery.

- **An unrelated restart creates a false positive.**  
  Mitigation: require an increase in the exact durable-specific log message, advanced restart metadata, and a newly created durable.

- **Docker logs contain an older matching message.**  
  Mitigation: compare the exact message count before and after deletion rather than searching for mere presence.

- **The durable is recreated before the test can observe its absence.**  
  Mitigation: absence is not an assertion. Successful deletion plus a later `ConsumerInfo.Created` proves deletion/recreation without racing the gap.

- **Docker restart backoff delays recovery in CI.**  
  Mitigation: use a 20-second recovery ceiling, report container state and logs, and retain the cleanup fallback.

- **A RED mutation leaves Access running without its durable.**  
  Mitigation: cleanup checks both durable existence and readiness, force-restarts the container when either is missing, then waits for quiescence.

- **Replay mutates lifecycle state or slows the suite.**  
  Mitigation: delete only `access-slot-policy`, keep this test first, and require its replay backlog to drain before proceeding.

- **Later changes add publications before this test.**  
  Mitigation: retain an explicit comment that source placement is operationally significant. Policy replay remains envelope-idempotent, and the pending/ready postcondition catches failure to converge.

- **Aggressive Docker polling adds overhead.**  
  Mitigation: use 250-millisecond polling only during the short reaction window, then 500-millisecond recovery sampling; do not invoke the existing two-second `retry` where it would impose unnecessary latency.

## 7. Out of scope

- Exposing Access on a host port or adding `SMOKE_ACCESS_URL`.
- Making the transient 503 window longer for testability.
- Deleting `access-ticket-issuer` or both Access durables.
- Re-testing every other cause of `ConsumeContext.Closed()`.
- Changing restart policy, readiness semantics, or `waitConsume`.
- Adding a new ADR; this plan follows ADR-017.
- Adding an opt-in test mode or altering `scripts/smoke.sh`.
- Adding separate lifecycle assertions: the existing smoke tail’s `verify-lifecycle` remains the safety net.
